speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent. You mentioned fever and altered mentation for two days; have you experienced any seizures, severe headache, or neck stiffness? Also, have you had any recent insect bites or travel to a tropical area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Are you currently on any other medications besides haloperidol, and have you noticed any skin rash, confusion, or hallucinations recently? Also, please describe the nature of your altered mentation; is it lethargy, agitation, or incoherence?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, and Serum Drug Levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of tics, currently on a low dose of haloperidol. Social history: Patient details on social and occupational history not provided.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, abdominal pain, loose stools, burning micturition, or seizures. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol; fever and altered mentation are not typical presentations of migraine. I need to know if you have had any recent exposure to new foods, medications, or if anyone in your household has become ill. Also, can you confirm if the altered mentation involves confusion or incoherence?

REQUEST TEST: Blood Cultures, Arthrocentesis (if joint swelling is present), and Toxicology Screen.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Haloperidol-induced Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) with possible superimposed encephalitis.
